messages:
incident-bot: Paging: Sev2 — multiple customer reports of timeouts for large file uploads from eu-west-1 private subnets to the internet via NAT gateway. Please acknowledge and join #incidents.
Emma (oncall): acked, I'm on it. starting a quick blast radius check. @Raj can you pull route table and NAT health for the affected subnets?
Raj (netops): looking now. seeing high packet drop counters on the NAT gateway metrics and a spike in TCP retransmits from the private subnets. NAT gateway CPU fine, but ENI tx errors up.
Sophie (eng-sre): any recent infra changes? Terraform apply earlier today touched a transit firewall in the eu-west transit VPC — possible MTU or iptables change.
Emma (oncall): good flag. @Jamal - CS — any customer-facing alerts sent? We should be careful; some customers are already DMing support.
Jamal - CS: we've put an interim banner on status.redwood.ai: "Intermittent upload failures in eu-west-1". Customers reporting ~10-30% failed large uploads, small requests unaffected.
Datadog-Bot: Alert: high tcp_retransmit_rate on nat-gw-03 (eu-west-1) — 175% over baseline. Link: https://dd.example.com/alerts/98765
Raj (netops): pulling route tables: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=rw-eu-private-*` shows all private subnets pointed to nat-gw-03. No recent route changes recorded in config history for those RTs.
Sophie (eng-sre): checking NACLs/security groups: no deny rules added. But I see a recent change on the transit firewall appliance: MTU lowered from 1500 -> 1400 in a rollout at 09:12 UTC per deploy logs. That can cause PMTU blackholing for TCP flows with DF bit.
Emma (oncall): that matches symptom: small requests (no fragmentation) fine, large uploads stall. Can we test PMTU behaviour from a private instance via netcat and increasing payload sizes?
Raj (netops): running quick test from a repro instance in subnet-priv-eu-1a: `ping -M do -s 1472 8.8.8.8` -> returns "Frag needed but DF set"? getting ICMP unreachable intermittently. That indicates PMTU path issue.
Sophie (eng-sre): transit firewall is dropping ICMP "Fragmentation Needed" responses or rewriting MTU. Also NAT healthchecks rely on ICMP/eph ports — if ICMP blocked, some stacks interpret as failure and trigger failover loops.
Emma (oncall): mitigation options: 1) revert MTU change on transit firewall (fast but touches that device), 2) adjust NAT gateway path to use alternate AZ/standby appliance, 3) implement temporary MSS clamping on the egress NAT/elastic load balancer to avoid DF fragmentation.
Raj (netops): I can push an MSS clamp on the transit firewall as a quick fix to 1360. Command on appliance: `set firewall flow tcp-mss-clamp 1360` — doing a dry-run.
Sophie (eng-sre): while Raj applies clamp, I'll open a canary route to nat-gw-04 (in eu-west-1b) and shift 5% of traffic via route table weight alias to test failover without full cutover.
Raj (netops): applied MSS clamp. Monitoring.
Datadog-Bot: Metric update: tcp_retransmit_rate on nat-gw-03 decreased 60% in last 30s.
Emma (oncall): visible improvement on customer repro tests. Uploads that previously failed now proceed in canary tests. @Jamal can you update the status page with "Mitigation in progress: MSS clamping applied; routing canary enabled" and note potential ETA ~30m?
Jamal - CS: updated status page and sent proactive messages to top affected customers. Marked as investigating -> partial mitigation.
Sophie (eng-sre): can we keep MSS clamp for now and schedule a rollback of the transit MTU change after change control? We need a proper postmortem. Also check NAT gateway failover logs — there were some transient healthchecks flapping due to ICMP being filtered.
Raj (netops): confirmed NAT healthchecks were timing out when ICMP was blocked -> triggered re-attachment of ENIs in some cases. That's why we saw ENI tx errors and transient loss. MSS clamp prevented fragmentation, so less retransmits, and healthchecks stabilized.
Emma (oncall): severity to Sev3 now since mitigation reduced customer impact but still ongoing for full rollback. Assigning postmortem to Sophie. Timeline notes: initial deploy (MTU change) 09:12 UTC; alerts start 09:25; oncall paged 09:28; MSS clamp applied 09:46; canary routing 09:50; observed stabilization 09:53.
Sophie (eng-sre): I'll own the RCA and follow-up: include change coordination gaps, missing automated test for PMTU, and add monitoring for ICMP unreachable rates. Also will propose adding an automated canary after tunnel/firewall MTU changes.
Raj (netops): follow-ups from me: revert the MTU change on firewall in a maintenance window, verify path MTU end-to-end, and add NAT healthcheck fallbacks that don't rely solely on ICMP.
Jamal - CS: customers updated, we offered temporary workarounds for customers with custom VPN appliances (lower MSS at client end). No escalations so far.
Emma (oncall): handoff to day shifter @Sophie in 40m for incident cleanup. I'll update the incident record and close paging. Thanks all for quick response :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident note appended to ticket INC-2026-341: "PMTU blackhole due to transit firewall MTU change leading to NAT healthcheck flapping and packet drops. Mitigated by MSS clamping and route canary. Owner: Sophie (eng-sre)."
Sophie (eng-sre): acked. I'll follow up with a postmortem draft and action items. Leaving monitoring on for 2 hours.
Emma (oncall): closing active paging. Stand by for postmortem review later today.
